title: Taiwan's Legislature Lets AI Read Bills Aloud for the First Time
summaryZh: 立法院首度用AI朗讀法案，70分鐘唸完15份提案。
summaryHi: ताइवान की संसद ने पहली बार विधेयक पढ़ने के लिए AI का इस्तेमाल किया; 15 प्रस्ताव 70 मिनट में पढ़े गए।
summaryEs: El Parlamento de Taiwán usa por primera vez la IA para leer proyectos de ley en voz alta.
summaryJa: 立法院が初めてAIで法案を読み上げ、15件を70分で完了。
summaryKo: 대만 입법원, 처음으로 AI가 법안 낭독… 15건을 70분 만에 마쳐.
summaryEn: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan used an AI voice to read 15 draft bills aloud for the first time, finishing in 70 minutes.
paragraphs: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan has, for the first time, handed one of its most routine tasks to artificial intelligence. On Wednesday, an AI voice read proposed legislation aloud to a committee, a job normally done by legislative staff.

Reading bills aloud is a formal step that must take place before a committee can begin reviewing them. The Social Welfare and Environmental Hygiene Committee faced 15 separate versions of proposed amendments to the Dementia Basic Act, and members agreed to let the AI take over.

The system started at one and a half times normal speed. After 10 minutes, lawmakers confirmed they could still follow, so the pace was raised to double speed. The entire reading was completed in 70 minutes.

Committee chair Chen Ching-hui of the Kuomintang said staff would have needed roughly two hours and 11 minutes to get through all the proposals. She said she hoped the approach would be adopted more widely. The committee had tested the application with the Legislature's information technology department in advance to check its accuracy.

Chen is no stranger to the technology. In 2024, after losing her voice, she used an AI-generated copy of it to question Premier Cho Jung-tai during a plenary session. Legislative Speaker Han Kuo-yu has encouraged lawmakers to explore AI and has set up a task force to study possible uses.
Taiwan's parliament, the Legislative Yuan, tried something new on 11 November. For the first time, a computer program with AI read new law ideas out loud.

Before lawmakers talk about a new law, someone must read the proposals to them. This is a normal step. A committee had 15 proposals to change a law about dementia. Dementia is an illness that makes people forget things.
The AI started reading at 1.5 times normal speed. After 10 minutes, the lawmakers said they could follow it. So the AI read even faster, at two times normal speed. It finished in 70 minutes.
The committee chair, Chen Ching-hui, said people would need about two hours and 11 minutes to read everything. She wants the parliament to use AI more.
In 2024, Chen lost her voice. She used an AI copy of her own voice to ask the premier questions. Speaker Han Kuo-yu also wants lawmakers to try AI.

這是第一次由具備人工智慧的電腦程式把新的法律提案大聲唸出來。

這是一般的步驟。
某委員會有15份修改失智症相關法律的提案。

AI一開始以1.5倍的正常速度朗讀。
10分鐘後，立委表示他們跟得上。
於是AI唸得更快，用兩倍速朗讀。
它在70分鐘內唸完。
委員會召集委員陳菁徽說，人工朗讀全部內容大約需要2小時11分鐘。
她希望立法院多使用AI。
2024年，陳菁徽失聲了。

paragraphs: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan used artificial intelligence (AI) to read proposed laws aloud for the first time on Wednesday, 11 November. Lawmakers say the test saved a lot of time.

Reading bills aloud is a standard step before a committee reviews them. On Wednesday, the Social Welfare and Environmental Hygiene Committee had to deal with 15 different versions of changes to the Dementia Basic Act. The committee agreed to let an AI voice do the reading instead of staff.
The AI began at 1.5 times normal speed. After about 10 minutes, lawmakers said they could still keep up, so it was made to read at double speed. The whole reading took 70 minutes.

Committee chair Chen Ching-hui, of the Kuomintang (KMT), said staff would have needed about two hours and 11 minutes to read all 15 proposals. She hopes the system will be used more widely. Before the meeting, the committee tested the tool with the Legislature's information technology department to make sure it read accurately.

Chen has used AI in parliament before. In 2024, when she lost her voice, she questioned Premier Cho Jung-tai with an AI version of her own voice. Speaker Han Kuo-yu has also set up a task force to study how AI could help the Legislature.

朗讀法案是委員會審查前的標準步驟。

委員會同意由AI語音代替職員朗讀。
AI一開始以1.5倍的正常速度朗讀。
大約10分鐘後，立委表示仍然跟得上，於是改用兩倍速朗讀。
整個朗讀花了70分鐘。
國民黨（KMT）籍召集委員陳菁徽說，職員朗讀全部15份提案大約需要2小時11分鐘。
她希望這套系統能更廣泛地使用。
會議之前，委員會已和立法院資訊部門一起測試這個工具，確保它唸得準確。
陳菁徽以前就在國會用過AI。
2024年她失聲時，曾用AI生成的自己的聲音質詢行政院長卓榮泰。
立法院長韓國瑜也成立了專案小組，研究AI如何協助立法院。

paragraphs: In a modest but symbolic break with parliamentary tradition, Taiwan's Legislative Yuan on Wednesday allowed artificial intelligence to perform a task long carried out by human clerks: reading draft legislation aloud before committee review.

The formal reading is a procedural requirement that precedes any detailed scrutiny of a bill. Confronted with 15 competing versions of amendments to the Dementia Basic Act, the Social Welfare and Environmental Hygiene Committee agreed to let an AI voice handle the recitation.

The software initially read at one and a half times normal speed. Once lawmakers indicated, after 10 minutes, that they were comfortably keeping pace, it was accelerated to double speed, finishing the entire batch in 70 minutes.

Committee convener Chen Ching-hui, a Kuomintang legislator, estimated that staff would have required about two hours and 11 minutes for the same material, and expressed hope that the practice would spread. The committee had trialled the application beforehand with the Legislature's information technology department to verify its accuracy.

Chen has a personal stake in the technology. In 2024, having temporarily lost her voice, she interpellated Premier Cho Jung-tai using an AI-generated replica of it. Speaker Han Kuo-yu has likewise urged the chamber to embrace AI, establishing a task force to examine its potential applications.
sentZh: 台灣立法院週三打破議會傳統，雖然幅度不大卻具象徵意義：讓人工智慧執行長期由人工書記負責的工作──在委員會審查前朗讀法案草案。
正式朗讀是任何法案進入詳細審查前的程序要求。
面對《失智症基本法》15個互相競爭的修正版本，社會福利及衛生環境委員會同意由AI語音負責朗讀。
軟體起初以1.5倍正常速度朗讀。
10分鐘後，立委表示能輕鬆跟上，於是加速到兩倍速，70分鐘就唸完全部內容。
召集委員、國民黨立委陳菁徽估計，職員唸同樣的內容需要大約2小時11分鐘，並表示希望這種做法能推廣開來。
委員會事先已與立法院資訊部門試用這套應用程式，以確認其準確度。
陳菁徽與這項技術有切身關係。
2024年她暫時失聲時，曾用AI生成的聲音複製品質詢行政院長卓榮泰。
立法院長韓國瑜同樣敦促議會擁抱AI，並成立專案小組研究其潛在應用。

paragraphs: Taiwan's Legislative Yuan has taken a small but telling step towards automating parliamentary procedure. On Wednesday, for the first time, an artificial intelligence system was entrusted with reading proposed legislation aloud, a duty traditionally performed by legislative staff.

The reading of bills is an obligatory formality that must be completed before substantive committee deliberation can commence. Faced with 15 rival drafts amending the Dementia Basic Act, members of the Social Welfare and Environmental Hygiene Committee consented to delegate the task to an AI voice.

The system began at one and a half times conventional speed. After 10 minutes, legislators confirmed that comprehension was not compromised, and the rate was subsequently doubled. The recitation concluded in 70 minutes, considerably faster than a human reader could have managed.

According to committee convener Chen Ching-hui of the Kuomintang, staff would have needed approximately two hours and 11 minutes to cover the same proposals. She advocated broader adoption of the tool, which had been rigorously tested in advance with the Legislature's information technology department to ensure accuracy.

Chen's enthusiasm is rooted in experience: in 2024, after losing her voice, she questioned Premier Cho Jung-tai with an AI-generated rendition of it. Meanwhile, Speaker Han Kuo-yu has encouraged the chamber to explore the technology and has convened a task force to assess its prospective applications.
sentZh: 台灣立法院在議事程序自動化上，邁出了雖小卻意義深遠的一步。
週三，人工智慧系統首次受託朗讀法律提案，而這項職責傳統上由立法院職員執行。
朗讀法案是實質委員會審議開始前必須完成的例行手續。
面對15份修正《失智症基本法》的互相競爭草案，社會福利及衛生環境委員會的委員同意把這項工作交給AI語音。
系統一開始以1.5倍的一般速度朗讀。
10分鐘後，立委確認理解並未受影響，隨後速度便加倍。
朗讀在70分鐘內結束，比人工朗讀快得多。
據國民黨籍召集委員陳菁徽表示，職員唸完同樣的提案約需2小時11分鐘。
她主張更廣泛地採用這項工具；該工具事先已與立法院資訊部門經過嚴格測試，以確保準確。
陳菁徽的熱忱源自親身經驗：2024年她失聲後，曾以AI生成的聲音版本質詢行政院長卓榮泰。
與此同時，立法院長韓國瑜鼓勵議會探索這項技術，並召集專案小組評估其未來應用。
